issues.hypothesis: Hash-join builds over 1M rows are expensive per row, even with no probe. q03's o_orderkey HJ costs 0.20s CPU when the probe side is empty: count(*) with l_shipdate > 1998-11-30 gives 0 probe rows, and the build has 1.45M rows, so that is about 137ns per build row. Payload width does not matter: count(*) costs the same as the full q03 payload. In hot q03 the HJ is 0.38s of 1.08s user. In hot q09 the o_orderkey=l_orderkey HJ (3.27M-row build) is 0.80s of 2.65s user, the largest operator. The pointer table is NextPowerOfTwo(count*load_factor) entries, i.e. 4M x 8B = 32MB for q03. InsertHashesLoop (join_hashtable.cpp:591) linear-probes at slot = hash & bitmask, the LOW hash bits. The sink, however, radix-partitions on HIGH bits: RadixPartitioning::Shift/Mask, the bits just below the 16-bit salt. Each finalize task's chunk range therefore scatters inserts over the whole 32MB table, roughly one cache/TLB miss per row. If the slot index is the top log2(capacity) bits below the salt, i.e. slot = (hash >> (48 - log2cap)) & bitmask, the slot's top bits equal the radix partition bits. Every partition then owns a contiguous capacity/2^radix_bits region (2MB for q03), and a finalize task working inside one partition writes L2/L3-resident memory.
issues.plan: 1) First verify cheaply with a temporary timer or a perf breakdown that the finalize insert dominates the build CPU on the q03 build-only micro (shown in memory). If sink append dominates instead, stop and report. 2) In JoinHashTable (src/include/duckdb/execution/join_hashtable.hpp and src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp), add a member `slot_shift`, set in InitializePointerTable/AllocatePointerTable (~line 787-817). For the in-memory single-round path, use 48 - log2(capacity), clamped at >= 0. For the external/partitioned-round path (PrepareExternalFinalize, physical_hash_join.cpp ~1244 sets EXTERNAL_LOAD_FACTOR), keep 0, i.e. today's low bits. A round holds only a subset of partitions, so high-bit slots would cluster there. 3) Apply the shift everywhere a slot is derived: ApplyBitmaskAndGetSaltBuild, the probe-side bitmask application (~line 151-161, GetRowPointers and the salt/offset code), and any other `& bitmask` use (grep it). Linear-probe wrap-around stays `& bitmask`. The salt stays the top 16 bits. 4) Make the finalize tasks (physical_hash_join.cpp, the parallel finalize with chunks_per_task) iterate chunks in partition order. Check that data_collection is combined partition by partition. If it is not, combine it that way, or give each task a single partition's chunk range. 5) Correctness checks: INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/SEMI/ANTI/MARK joins, NULL keys, a forced external join (small memory_limit), duplicate-heavy keys, and both sides of PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD.
issues.expected_gain: Builds over 1M rows. q03 HJ 0.38s→~0.25s (-5..-10%); q09 orderkey HJ 0.80s (-5..-8%); smaller gains on q05/q07/q08/q18/q21-like plans. Estimated geomean -2..-4% if the finalize-insert share is as large as the miss model predicts.
issues.generality: Any in-memory hash join whose pointer table is larger than L2/L3 (>~500K build rows), which covers most fact-to-dimension and fact-to-fact joins. Small builds are unchanged, since their table fits in cache either way. The external path is left as is.
issues.risk: Medium-high. Slot addressing must be identical on build and probe, or rows will be missed: test every join type and the external path. A poor hash high-bit distribution could lengthen probe chains, but DuckDB hashes are murmur-mixed. If the finalize share is small, the gain is too, so step 1 gates the work.
